description: The >>DEFINE compilation-variable-name AS { literal | arithmetic-expression | PARAMETER | OFF } [OVERRIDE] compiler directive (ISO §2023:7.3.11) - it defines the compilation variables the §2023:7.3.16 IF and §2023:7.3.13 EVALUATE directives and §2023:13.10 constant entries read. Implemented by ConditionalCompilationProcessor; the introduction gate rejects the directive word below 2002. The §2023:7.3 compiler-directive facility is a COBOL-2002 introduction: COBOL-85 has no compiler directives at all, so a '>>' line cannot occur in a conforming COBOL-85 source. The edition edge below 2023 is DERIVED, not quoted (VCR Table 7's discipline, rows 7.19/7.20 - the repo holds no 2002 or 2014 text, ratified decision #1): the derivation is (a) the M2 post-85 feature catalog in docs/ISO2023_CONFORMANCE_PLAN.md, which places '*>' inline comments, >>SOURCE FORMAT, conditional compilation and 'recognize-and-ignore of the other standard >> directives' in COBOL-2002, (b) the sibling row leap-second-directive-2002, already landed on the same derivation (kb/Work PB65), and (c) Annex E, which itemizes the 2014->2023 delta and does NOT list this directive among the additions, so it predates 2023. Overturnable in one line if the 2002/2014 text is ever acquired.
citation: ISO §2023:7.3.11; the §2023:7.3 compiler-directive facility is a COBOL-2002 introduction (M2 catalog derivation, VCR Table 7 discipline)

directiveOperand.citation: ISO §2023:7.3.11.2 general format + §2023:7.3.11.3: a compilation-variable-name with AS / OFF / PARAMETER / OVERRIDE and a compile-time expression — diagnosed by the conditional-compilation driver as COBOL1618/COBOL1619.
